newsitem.title: GREECE: DRACHMA TO SLIP BY ABOUT 1.0PCT VS ECU IN 97 - BARCLAYS.
newsitem.headline: DRACHMA TO SLIP BY ABOUT 1.0PCT VS ECU IN 97 - BARCLAYS.

text.p: The drachma's depreciation against the ecu this year will be very similar to its 1.0 percent slide in 1996 and ecu/drachma is projected to reach 312 in November 1997, said Barclays, London.
"The drachma depreciated by only 1.0 percent against the ecu during 1996 and we expect a very similar outcome for 1997," it said in its May international financial report.
Ecu/drachma is projected to settle at 312 and mark/drachma at 159 in November 1997, said Barclays.
Spot ecu/drachma settled at 311.20 and mark/drachma at 159.480 in the central bank's fixing on Wednesday.

"The hard drachma policy will result in a continuing loss of external competitiveness but disinflation is currently being given much higher priority and exchange rate stability is the principal weapon," it said.
Greece's current account balance posted a deficit of $21 million in January from a surplus of $363.7 million in the same month a year ago according to central bank figures.

Bank of Greece is expected to adopt a new methodology for balance of payments accounting based on a resident versus non-resident breakdown. The current methodology is based on the currency of transaction.
Analysts expect the new methodology to improve the trade balance by as much as 350 billion drachmas by including exports to the Balkans denominated in drachmas.

Headline inflation eased to 5.9 percent year-on-year in April from 6.0 percent in March. Core inflation which does not include food and energy prices was unchanged at 7.5 percent in April accroding to private estimates.
The central bank would almost certainly be prepared to raise rates sharply in the face of unwanted pressure on the drachma, it added.
But Barclays expected the three-month Greek-German rate differential to narrow further in the next few months provided a benign environment.
"If things continue to go well, could be less than 6.0 percent by the end of forecast period (May 1998)," it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
